caption: The drawing depicts a pair of tall, weathered wooden doors, each door featuring three prominent rectangular panels with raised octagonal shapes in their centers, accented by metal studs. The color of the doors is faded and worn, with variations of light grayish-brown, beige, and traces of darker brown indicating aged wood and chipped paint. The doors are set in a stone or stucco arched doorway, with the arch itself outlined by pinkish and reddish hues and adorned above by intricate, white ornamental stucco scrollwork and floriated detailing. Some parts of the stucco surrounding the arch are missing, revealing reddish-brown bricks underneath, especially on the left and right sides of the doorway. The doors rest above two grayish stone steps, with a cobblestone pathway visible at the bottom of the composition. The background of the image is off-white, with the objects artfully centered and the edges fading smoothly into the blank space. The signature “Juanita Delmonte” appears in small red letters near the bottom right of the steps.
title: Doorway and Wall Painting
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
